evidence.V1: Front and three-quarter silhouettes read clearly as a round-headed arch module; top view is a plain rectangle, which is expected and fine for a 2-stud-deep wall piece.
evidence.V2: Piers have three block courses, voussoir ring and gold keystone give medium/small detail, but the whole upper half is one blank flat slab with only a thin top cap, so the hierarchy is lopsided.
evidence.V3: Straight vertical piers, flat rectangular wall and a narrow arch opening with even-sized blocks read as stiff primitives; no stylised taper, chunky imposts or uneven stone sizes.
evidence.V4: Uniform chamfers on pier blocks, voussoirs, keystone and top cap catch the light consistently in the springing and end-section close-ups.
evidence.V5: Studio and flat close-ups are clean: no pinches, z-fighting or stray faceting at the springing, keystone or end section.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in three values (light imposts, mid courses, dark plinth course) plus a single gold keystone accent: disciplined.
evidence.V7: 660 tris vs module target 800 / ceiling 2000: under target.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, stone hue with gold keystone accent per the modular spec, kit-width chamfers; colourways (brick, sandstone) swap cleanly.
evidence.V9: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default keeps the opening walkable, CanTouch off, MeshPart.Color white, grid-corner origin, T1 tiling pass: correct.

top_fixes: Break up the blank upper wall: add block coursing, a string course or visible spandrel stones so the top half carries medium detail
Give the arch a more stylised proportion: wider opening, chunkier projecting imposts/keystone, slightly varied block sizes
Make the keystone project and taper more strongly so the gold accent reads at 64 px
